title: Food & Writing Posts
description: From your course: words for describing food and its taste and texture, kitchen basics, and the language of writing captions and posts.

items.definition: simple, familiar food that makes you feel better when you are sad or tired
items.example: Mac and cheese is my go-to [comfort food] after a bad day at work.
items.exampleRu: Макароны с сыром — моя любимая еда для поднятия настроения после тяжёлого дня на работе.
items.trap: Not 'comfortable food': 'comfortable' describes chairs, clothes and people, not food.

items.definition: substances in food like bread, rice and pasta that give your body energy
items.example: My personal trainer says I need more complex [carbohydrates], like oats and brown rice.
items.exampleRu: Мой тренер говорит, что мне нужно больше сложных углеводов — например, овсянки и бурого риса.
items.trap: In everyday speech people say 'carbs'; 'hydrocarbons' (углеводороды) are oil and gas, not food.

items.definition: a very important part or quality that something must have
items.example: Fast Wi-Fi is an [essential feature] of any café I work from.
items.exampleRu: Быстрый вайфай — обязательное условие для любого кафе, где я работаю.
items.trap: Черта is 'feature' for things and places, 'trait' for a person's character, and 'line' only for a drawn line.

items.definition: round, light brown beans used to make hummus and curries
items.example: Hummus is so easy – just blitz a tin of [chickpeas] with garlic and tahini.
items.exampleRu: Хумус готовится элементарно: просто взбейте в блендере банку нута с чесноком и тахини.
collocations: a tin of chickpeas (US: a can)
items.trap: Нут is 'chickpeas', not 'nut' (a nut is орех); Americans also call them 'garbanzo beans'.

items.definition: small balls of dough cooked in hot oil, often eaten as a snack or dessert
items.example: At the street food market, I got a bag of [fried doughballs] dusted with sugar.
items.exampleRu: На фуд-маркете я купил пакетик жареных шариков из теста, посыпанных сахаром.
items.trap: Жареный is 'fried' when cooked in oil; 'roasted' means cooked in the oven and 'grilled' on a grill.

items.definition: how good food tastes and how attractive it looks or seems
items.example: Nothing beats the [taste and appeal] of home cooking after a week of takeaways.
items.exampleRu: После недели еды навынос ничто не сравнится со вкусом и притягательностью домашней кухни.
items.trap: 'Appeal' here is a noun (what makes something attractive); the adjective is 'appealing'.

items.definition: having a layer of oil all over it
items.example: The chips at that place are always [covered in oil], so I usually skip them.
items.exampleRu: Картошка фри в том месте вечно вся в масле, так что я обычно её не заказываю.
items.trap: Say 'covered in' or 'covered with', not 'covered by'; and масло for frying is 'oil', while масло for bread is 'butter'.

items.definition: containing or covered in a lot of oil
items.example: My doctor says I should eat [oily] fish like salmon twice a week.
items.exampleRu: Врач говорит, что мне нужно есть жирную рыбу, например лосося, два раза в неделю.
items.trap: Жирная рыба is 'oily fish', not 'fat fish'; 'oiled' means oil was put on it (an oiled bike chain).

items.definition: having a strong, hot taste from spices or chilli
items.example: Is this curry very [spicy]? I can't handle anything too hot.
items.exampleRu: Это карри сильно острое? Я плохо переношу острую еду.
items.trap: Острая еда is 'spicy' or 'hot', never 'sharp' (a knife is sharp); 'hot' can also mean горячий, so 'spicy' is clearer.

items.definition: smooth and rich, like cream or containing cream
items.example: I'll take [creamy] milk chocolate over dark chocolate any day.
items.exampleRu: Я всегда выберу нежный молочный шоколад, а не тёмный.
items.trap: Крем-суп is usually 'cream of mushroom soup' or 'a creamy soup'; 'creamed' is for food cooked with cream (creamed spinach).

items.definition: pleasantly hard and dry on the outside so it breaks easily, often after frying or baking
items.example: Roast potatoes should be [crispy] on the outside and fluffy inside.
items.exampleRu: Запечённая картошка должна быть хрустящей снаружи и рассыпчатой внутри.
items.trap: Crispy is light and dry, usually after frying or baking (crispy bacon); crunchy is firm and loud when you bite (crunchy apples, crunchy crackers).

items.definition: firm and making a loud noise when you bite it
items.example: I keep [crunchy] carrot sticks at my desk so I don't snack on crisps.
items.exampleRu: Я держу на рабочем столе хрустящие морковные палочки, чтобы не таскать чипсы.
items.trap: Crunchy = firm and noisy (raw carrots, nuts, crackers); crispy = light and dry after frying or baking (bacon, chips). In the UK, 'crisps' are чипсы.

items.definition: containing too much fat or oil, in an unpleasant way
items.example: Honestly, a [greasy] fry-up is the best cure for a hangover.
items.exampleRu: Честно говоря, жирная яичница с беконом — лучшее средство от похмелья.
items.trap: Жирная еда is 'greasy' (too much oil, negative) or 'fatty' (lots of fat); 'fat' as an adjective describes a body, not food.

items.definition: soft, sticky and melted, usually in a nice way
items.example: The best brownies are still a bit [gooey] in the middle.
items.exampleRu: Лучшие брауни — те, что внутри ещё чуть тягучие.
items.trap: Gooey is informal and usually positive about food; 'viscous' is a scientific word for liquids.

items.definition: containing a lot of sugar, often too much
items.example: I'm trying to cut down on [sugary] drinks, so it's mostly water and tea now.
items.exampleRu: Я стараюсь пить меньше сладких напитков, так что теперь в основном вода и чай.
items.trap: 'Sweet' is a neutral or positive taste; 'sugary' stresses that there is a lot of sugar, often in a negative way.

items.definition: a soft yellow fat made from milk that you put on bread or use in cooking
items.example: Toast just isn't the same without a bit of salted [butter].
items.exampleRu: Тост без кусочка солёного сливочного масла — совсем не то.
items.trap: Масло is 'butter' (made from milk) or 'oil' (olive oil, sunflower oil); сливочное масло is just 'butter', never 'cream oil'.

items.definition: a solid food made from milk
items.example: Be honest – do I put too much [cheese] on my pasta?
items.exampleRu: Скажи честно, я слишком много сыра кладу в пасту?
items.trap: Cheese is usually uncountable (some cheese, a slice of cheese); 'cheeses' means different kinds of cheese.

items.definition: the thick, fatty part of milk; also a soft substance you put on your skin
items.example: In summer, I could live on strawberries and [cream].
items.exampleRu: Летом могу хоть каждый день есть клубнику со сливками.
items.trap: Сливки is plural in Russian, but 'cream' is uncountable: 'some cream', not 'some creams'.

items.definition: a mix of flour and water that you use to make bread or pizza
items.example: Let the pizza [dough] rest for an hour before you roll it out.
items.exampleRu: Дай тесту для пиццы постоять час, прежде чем раскатывать.
items.trap: Тесто is 'dough' for bread and pizza, 'pastry' for pies and tarts, and 'batter' for pancakes; the 'gh' is silent.

items.definition: a sour yellow fruit
items.example: Could I have a sparkling water with ice and a slice of [lemon], please?
items.exampleRu: Можно мне газированную воду со льдом и долькой лимона?
items.trap: In the UK 'lemonade' usually means a sweet fizzy drink like Sprite, not fresh lemon juice.

items.definition: a plant with a fresh, cool taste and smell
items.example: A fresh [mint] tea is perfect after a heavy meal.
items.exampleRu: Свежий мятный чай — то, что надо после сытного обеда.
items.trap: The herb is uncountable (some mint), but 'a mint' is a small sweet; 'minty' means tasting of mint.

items.definition: dry fruits with a hard shell, like walnuts or almonds
items.example: Sorry, I can't eat that – I'm allergic to [nuts].
items.exampleRu: Извините, мне это нельзя — у меня аллергия на орехи.
items.trap: Say 'allergic to nuts' (plural, with 'to'), not 'allergic on nut'; informally 'nuts' also means crazy.

items.definition: a hot spice made from black or white seeds; also a red, green or yellow vegetable
items.example: Can you grab two red [peppers] and an onion on your way home?
items.exampleRu: Можешь захватить по дороге домой два красных перца и луковицу?
items.trap: The vegetable is 'a red/green pepper' (US: bell pepper) and is countable; the spice, black pepper, is uncountable.

items.definition: white grains you add to food to give it more taste
items.example: Pass the [salt], would you? These eggs are a bit bland.
items.exampleRu: Передай соль, пожалуйста. Яйца какие-то пресные.
collocations: take sth with a pinch of salt
items.trap: 'Salty' means it tastes of too much salt; 'salted' means salt was added (salted butter, salted peanuts).

items.definition: a sweet white or brown substance that you put in drinks and food
items.example: Do you take [sugar] in your tea, or just milk?
items.exampleRu: Тебе в чай положить сахар или только молоко?
items.trap: Sugar is uncountable, but in tea and coffee Brits count spoons: 'One sugar or two?'; the natural verb is 'take', not 'drink with'.

items.translation: «сморы» (десерт из жареного зефира, шоколада и крекеров)
items.definition: a campfire snack of toasted marshmallow and chocolate between two biscuits
items.example: We sat round the campfire making [s'mores] until the marshmallows ran out.
items.exampleRu: Мы сидели у костра и делали сморы, пока не кончились маршмеллоу.
items.trap: S'mores (from 'some more') are an American treat; in the UK people often use digestive biscuits instead of graham crackers.

items.definition: marshmallow that has become soft and runny from heat
items.example: By the end of the night, I had [melted marshmallow] all over my hoodie.
items.exampleRu: К концу вечера у меня вся толстовка была в растаявшем маршмеллоу.
items.trap: Use 'melted' for things made soft by heat; 'thawed' is only for frozen food (thawed chicken).

items.definition: thick, solid pieces of something
items.example: These cookies have massive [chunks of] dark chocolate in them – try one!
items.exampleRu: В этом печенье огромные кусочки тёмного шоколада — попробуй!
collocations: a big chunk of my salary
items.pattern: a chunk of sth / chunks of sth
items.trap: A chunk is a thick, solid piece; a slice is thin and flat, and a crumb is tiny. 'A big chunk of my time/salary' is also common.

items.definition: unpleasantly cold
items.example: On a [chilly] autumn night, all I want is a bowl of hot soup.
items.exampleRu: Холодным осенним вечером мне хочется только тарелку горячего супа.
items.trap: Don't mix up chilly (cold), chilli (a hot pepper) and chilled (cold from the fridge, or relaxed).

items.definition: the feeling of being warm, comfortable and relaxed
items.example: What I love about winter is the [cosiness] of a pub with a real fire.
items.exampleRu: Что я люблю зимой — так это уют паба с настоящим камином.
items.trap: In speech people usually use the adjective: 'It's so cosy here!' sounds more natural than the noun. US spelling: cozy, coziness.

items.definition: a short text under or next to a photo or picture
items.example: Thinking of a [caption] takes me longer than taking the actual photo.
items.exampleRu: Придумать подпись у меня занимает больше времени, чем сделать само фото.
items.trap: Подпись under a photo is a 'caption'; your name written by hand is a 'signature', and подписка is a 'subscription'.

items.definition: a friendly, informal way of writing, like normal speech
items.example: Our boss wants the company newsletter to have a more [conversational tone].
items.exampleRu: Начальник хочет, чтобы корпоративная рассылка была написана в более разговорном тоне.
items.trap: Use the adjective: 'a conversational tone', not 'a conversation tone'.

items.definition: short forms of words or phrases, like 'BRB' or 'etc.'
items.example: Half the [abbreviations] my teenage cousin uses in texts mean nothing to me.
items.exampleRu: Половина сокращений, которые мой кузен-подросток пишет в сообщениях, мне ни о чём не говорят.
items.pattern: X is short for Y / X stands for Y
items.trap: Сокращение of a word is an 'abbreviation'; fewer jobs or less money is a 'cut' or 'reduction'. To explain one, say 'BRB is short for "be right back"'.

items.definition: printed in thick, dark letters so that it stands out
items.example: Could you put the deadline [in bold] so nobody misses it?
items.exampleRu: Можешь выделить дедлайн жирным, чтобы его никто не пропустил?
items.trap: Жирный шрифт is 'bold', never 'fat'; say 'in bold' and 'in italics', but just 'underlined' (no 'in').

items.definition: special importance or attention given to something
items.example: This company puts a lot of [emphasis] on work-life balance, which is why I applied.
items.exampleRu: Эта компания делает большой акцент на балансе работы и личной жизни — поэтому мне и захотелось там работать.
items.pattern: put/place emphasis on sth; emphasise sth (no 'on')
items.trap: Делать акцент на is 'put emphasis on' or 'emphasise', not 'make an accent on'; the verb takes no 'on': 'emphasise teamwork'.

items.definition: a short text that gives only the main points
items.example: Would you mind sending me a quick [summary] of the meeting? I had to leave early.
items.exampleRu: Можешь скинуть мне краткое резюме встречи? Мне пришлось уйти пораньше.
items.trap: Резюме of a text or meeting is a 'summary'; a резюме for a job is a 'CV' (US: résumé). Don't confuse it with 'summery' (like summer).

items.definition: strange or funny because it is the opposite of what you expect
items.example: It's a bit [ironic] that I wrote my healthy-eating post with a doughnut in my hand.
items.exampleRu: Немного иронично, что пост о здоровом питании я писал с пончиком в руке.
items.trap: Ironic means 'the opposite of what you'd expect'; don't use it for 'sarcastic' (saying the opposite to mock someone).

items.definition: a coloured wax stick that children use for drawing
items.example: My niece drew me a birthday card with her new wax [crayons].
items.exampleRu: Племянница нарисовала мне открытку на день рождения своими новыми восковыми мелками.
items.trap: Детские мелки for paper are 'crayons'; 'chalk' is for a blackboard or the pavement and is usually uncountable.

items.definition: things you did regularly before and things you do regularly now
items.example: Writing about my [past and present habits] made me realise how much I've changed.
items.exampleRu: Когда я написал о своих прошлых и нынешних привычках, я понял, как сильно изменился.
items.pattern: used to / would + verb (past); be always + -ing (annoying present habit)
items.trap: For past habits use 'used to' or 'would' (I used to eat fast food every day), not 'I was used to eat'.
